b. ἠὲ Κλάρον: a place in Colophon consecrated to Apollo and having an oracle of the god, founded by Manto, daughter of Teiresias, or by a certain hero Clarus, as Theopompus (115 FGrH 346 J.) says. Neanthes (84 FGrH 42 J.) says that Apollo obtained the city by lot and that it was named from the lot (κλῆρος); or because there Poseidon, Zeus, and Hades cast lots. The authors of the Thebaid (Epigonoi fr. 4 Kink.) say that Manto, daughter of Teiresias, was sent to Delphi as an offering by the Epigoni, and in accordance with an oracle of Apollo she went out and met Rhacius, son of Lebes, a Mycenaean by descent. And she married him—for the oracle contained this, that she should marry whomever she met—and coming to Colophon and being distressed there, she wept because of the destruction of her fatherland.
